title_en: Organic Law of the National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution to improve the organizational and working systems of the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee, to safeguard and regulate the exercise of their functions and powers, to uphold and improve the system of people's congresses, and to ensure that the people are the masters of the country.
Article 2 The National People's Congress is the highest organ of state power. Its permanent organ is the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

Article 3 The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall uphold the leadership of the Communist Party of China, adhere to Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Theory of Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as their guide, and shall exercise their functions and powers in accordance with the Constitution and laws.

Article 4 The National People's Congress is elected through democratic elections, is responsible to the people, and is subject to their supervision.
The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall uphold whole-process democracy, always maintain close ties with the people, listen to their opinions and suggestions, reflect their will, and safeguard their rights and interests.

Article 5 The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall exercise the legislative power of the state, decide on major issues, supervise the implementation of the Constitution and laws, uphold the unity, dignity, and authority of the socialist legal system, and build a socialist country under the rule of law.

Article 6 The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall practice the principle of democratic centralism, give full play to democracy, and exercise their functions and powers collectively.

Article 7 The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall actively engage in foreign exchanges and strengthen exchanges and cooperation with parliaments of other countries and international and regional parliamentary organizations.

Article 8 The National People's Congress shall serve a term of five years.
A session of the National People's Congress shall be held once a year and shall be convened by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may convene an interim session of the National People's Congress if it deems it necessary or if more than one-fifth of the deputies to the National People's Congress so propose.

Article 9 After the deputies to the National People's Congress are elected, their qualifications shall be examined by the Credentials Committee of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall, based on the report submitted by the Credentials Committee, confirm the qualifications of the deputies or determine that the election of certain deputies is invalid, and shall publish the list of deputies before the first session of each National People's Congress.
For by-elected deputies to the National People's Congress, the qualifications shall be examined in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 10 The deputies to the National People's Congress shall form delegations according to the electoral units. Each delegation shall respectively elect a head and deputy heads.
Before each session of the National People's Congress, the delegations shall discuss the preparatory matters for the session proposed by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. During the session, the delegations shall deliberate on various bills of the National People's Congress, and may, through the head of the delegation or a representative designated by the delegation, express opinions on the bills under deliberation at a meeting of the presidium or at a plenary session of the Congress.

Article 11 Before each session of the National People's Congress, a preparatory meeting shall be held to elect the presidium and the secretary-general for the current session and to adopt the agenda of the session and decisions on other preparatory matters.
The draft list of the presidium and the secretary-general shall be proposed by the Council of Chairpersons of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and, after deliberation and adoption at a meeting of the Standing Committee, shall be submitted to the preparatory meeting.

Article 12 The presidium shall preside over sessions of the National People's Congress.
The presidium shall elect a number of standing presidents to convene and preside over meetings of the presidium.
The presidium shall elect a number of its members to serve as executive chairmen for each plenary session of the Congress, and shall designate one of them to be the presiding officer of the plenary session.

Article 13 A secretariat shall be established for the session of the National People's Congress. The secretariat shall be composed of the secretary-general and a number of deputy secretaries-general. The candidates for deputy secretaries-general shall be decided by the presidium.
The secretariat, under the direction of the secretary-general, shall handle matters assigned by the presidium and manage the day-to-day work of the session. The deputy secretaries-general shall assist the secretary-general in his or her work.

Article 15 The standing presidents of the presidium shall, regarding matters to be submitted to the presidium for deliberation, hear reports from the secretariat and relevant special committees, and make suggestions to the presidium.
The standing presidents of the presidium may make necessary adjustments to the session agenda.

Article 16 The presidium of the National People's Congress, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the special committees of the National People's Congress, the State Council, the Central Military Commission, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, and the Supreme People's Procuratorate may submit to the National People's Congress bills that fall within the scope of its functions and powers.
Article 17 A delegation or a group of thirty or more deputies jointly may submit to the National People's Congress bills that fall within the scope of its functions and powers.

Article 18 The candidates for the Chairman, Vice-Chairmen, Secretary-General, and members of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the candidates for the President and Vice-President of the People's Republic of China, the candidate for the Chairman of the Central Military Commission, the candidate for the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, and the candidates for the President of the Supreme People's Court and the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall be nominated by the presidium. After deliberation and consultation among delegations, the presidium shall determine the list of formal candidates based on the opinions of the majority of deputies.

Article 19 The candidates for the Premier and other members of the State Council, and the candidates for members of the Central Military Commission other than the Chairman shall be nominated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Constitution.

Article 20 The presidium of the National People's Congress, three or more delegations, or one-tenth or more of the deputies may propose a bill for the recall of members of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the President or Vice-President of the People's Republic of China, members of the State Council and the Central Military Commission, the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, the President of the Supreme People's Court, or the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate. Such a bill shall be submitted by the presidium to the Congress for deliberation.

Article 21 During a session of the National People's Congress, a delegation or a group of thirty or more deputies jointly may submit in writing a question to the State Council or the departments under it, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, or the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 22 The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall be responsible to the National People's Congress and shall report on its work.
The term of office of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall be the same as that of the National People's Congress, and it shall exercise its functions and powers until a new Standing Committee is elected by the succeeding National People's Congress.

Article 23 The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall be composed of the following:
the Chairman,
a number of Vice-Chairmen,
the Secretary-General,
a number of members.
The members of the Standing Committee shall be elected by the National People's Congress from among its deputies.
No member of the Standing Committee shall hold any post in an administrative, supervisory, adjudicatory, or procuratorial organ of the state; if such a post is held, the member shall resign from the Standing Committee.

Article 24 The Chairman of the Standing Committee shall preside over the meetings and work of the Standing Committee. The Vice-Chairmen and the Secretary-General shall assist the Chairman in his or her work. The Vice-Chairmen may, upon entrustment by the Chairman, exercise part of the Chairman's functions and powers.
If the Chairman is unable to work due to health reasons or if the post of Chairman becomes vacant, the Standing Committee shall elect a Vice-Chairman to act as the Chairman until the Chairman recovers his or her health or until a new Chairman is elected by the National People's Congress.

Article 26 The Standing Committee shall establish a Credentials Committee.
The candidates for the chairperson, vice-chairpersons, and members of the Credentials Committee shall be nominated by the Council of Chairpersons from among the members of the Standing Committee, and the Standing Committee shall appoint or remove them.

Article 27 The Standing Committee shall establish a General Office, which shall work under the direction of the Secretary-General.
The Standing Committee shall have a number of Deputy Secretaries-General, who shall be appointed or removed by the Standing Committee upon the proposal of the Chairman.

Article 28 The Standing Committee shall establish a Legislative Affairs Commission, a Budgetary Affairs Commission, and other working commissions as needed.
The chairperson, vice-chairpersons, and members of the working commissions shall be appointed or removed by the Standing Committee upon the proposal of the Chairman.
The establishment, functions, and appointment and removal of members of the Committee for the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Committee for the Basic Law of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be governed by the relevant laws and decisions of the National People's Congress.

Article 29 The Council of Chairpersons, the special committees of the National People's Congress, the State Council, the Central Military Commission, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and a group of ten or more members of the Standing Committee jointly may submit to the Standing Committee bills that fall within the scope of its functions and powers.

Article 30 During a meeting of the Standing Committee, a group of ten or more members of the Standing Committee jointly may submit in writing a question to the State Council or the departments under it, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, or the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 31 When the National People's Congress is not in session, the Standing Committee may, upon nomination by the Premier of the State Council, decide on the appointment or removal of other members of the State Council; and upon nomination by the Chairman of the Central Military Commission, decide on the appointment or removal of other members of the Central Military Commission.

Article 32 When the National People's Congress is not in session, the Standing Committee may, upon the proposal of the Council of Chairpersons or the Premier of the State Council, decide to remove individual other members of the State Council; and upon the proposal of the Chairman of the Central Military Commission, decide to remove individual other members of the Central Military Commission.
Article 33 The Standing Committee must present a work report to the National People's Congress at each session of the Congress.

Article 34 The National People's Congress shall establish the Ethnic Affairs Committee, the Constitution and Law Committee, the Supervision and Judicial Committee, the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee, the Education, Science, Culture and Public Health Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, the Overseas Chinese Affairs Committee, the Environment and Resources Protection Committee, the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee, the Social Development Committee, and such other special committees as the National People's Congress deems necessary. Each special committee shall be under the leadership of the National People's Congress; when the Congress is not in session, it shall be under the leadership of its Standing Committee.
Each special committee shall be composed of a chairperson, a number of vice-chairpersons, and a number of members.
The candidates for chairperson, vice-chairpersons, and members of each special committee shall be nominated by the presidium from among the deputies and shall be voted on and adopted at a plenary meeting of the National People's Congress. When the Congress is not in session, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may appoint or remove the vice-chairpersons and members of the special committees, upon nomination by the Council of Chairpersons and after voting and adoption at a meeting of the Standing Committee.

Article 35 The term of office of each special committee shall be the same as that of the National People's Congress, and it shall perform its duties until a new special committee is elected by the succeeding National People's Congress.

Article 36 The chairperson of each special committee shall preside over the meetings and work of the committee. The vice-chairpersons shall assist the chairperson in his or her work.
Each special committee may, as needed, appoint a number of experts as advisers; advisers may attend meetings of the special committee and express opinions.
Advisers shall be appointed or removed by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

Article 38 The Ethnic Affairs Committee may conduct investigations and research on issues of strengthening ethnic unity and make suggestions; it shall deliberate on the autonomous regulations and separate regulations of autonomous regions submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for approval, and shall report to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

Article 39 The Constitution and Law Committee shall assume the responsibilities of promoting the implementation of the Constitution, conducting constitutional interpretation, advancing constitutional review, strengthening constitutional oversight, and cooperating in constitutional publicity.
The Constitution and Law Committee shall conduct unified deliberation on draft laws and draft decisions on legal issues submitted to the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee; other special committees shall provide opinions on the relevant drafts to the Constitution and Law Committee.

Article 40 The Financial and Economic Affairs Committee shall examine the draft national economic and social development plan, draft outline of the plan, draft central and local budgets, draft final accounts of the central government, and related reports and adjustment plans submitted by the State Council, and shall provide preliminary examination opinions and a report on the examination results; other special committees may provide opinions on the relevant drafts and reports to the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee.

Article 41 The National People's Congress or its Standing Committee may establish committees of inquiry into specific issues. The organization and work of such committees of inquiry shall be decided by the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee.

Article 42 The term of office of a deputy to the National People's Congress shall be five years, commencing from the first session of each National People's Congress and ending at the first session of the succeeding National People's Congress.

Article 43 Deputies to the National People's Congress must exemplarily abide by the Constitution and laws, keep state secrets, and assist in the implementation of the Constitution and laws in the production, work, and social activities in which they participate.

Article 44 Deputies to the National People's Congress shall maintain close ties with the electoral units that elected them and with the people; they may attend as non-voting delegates meetings of the people's congresses of the electoral units that elected them, hear and reflect the opinions and demands of the people through various means, strive to serve the people, and give full play to their role in whole-process democracy.

Article 45 The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the special committees and working commissions shall maintain close ties with deputies, hear their opinions and suggestions, support and ensure that deputies perform their duties according to law, expand deputies' participation in various work, and give full play to the role of deputies.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall establish and improve a working mechanism for members of the Standing Committee and the special committees and working commissions to maintain contact with deputies.
The administrative offices and working offices of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall provide services and guarantees for deputies to perform their duties.

Article 46 Suggestions, criticisms, and opinions concerning various aspects of work submitted by deputies to the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee shall be referred by the administrative offices of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to the relevant organs or organizations for study and handling, and the latter shall be responsible for replying.
With respect to suggestions, criticisms, and opinions submitted by deputies to the National People's Congress, the relevant organs or organizations shall communicate with the deputies, fully listen to their opinions, provide relevant information, seriously study and handle them, and promptly reply.
The relevant special committees of the National People's Congress and the administrative offices of the Standing Committee shall strengthen supervision and inspection of the handling work. The administrative offices of the Standing Committee shall report annually to the Standing Committee on the handling of deputies' suggestions, criticisms, and opinions, and shall make the information public.

Article 47 When deputies to the National People's Congress attend sessions of the Congress or perform other duties as deputies, the state shall provide them with appropriate subsidies and material conveniences as needed.

Article 48 No legal liability may be incurred for speeches or votes made by deputies to the National People's Congress or members of its Standing Committee at various meetings of the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee.

Article 49 No deputy to the National People's Congress may be arrested or subjected to criminal adjudication without the permission of the presidium of the National People's Congress or, when the Congress is not in session, without the permission of its Standing Committee.
If a deputy to the National People's Congress is detained on the spot as a flagrante delicto, the public security organ that executed the detention shall immediately report to the presidium of the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee.
